subject: Huge SE's when fitting colext models

messages.author: 326ae5da9dd7e9d7
messages.subject: Huge SE's when fitting colext models
parts:
Hi all,
 
I'm currently performing a multi-seasonal analysis on lizard presence/absence data over two years. Site-specific, observation-specific, and year-specific covariates are tested in a stepwise model selection approach. The goal of the study is to identify the factors influencing the occupancy, colonisation and extinction probabilities.
 
When I model the detection and occupancy probabilities as functions of observation- and site-specific covariates respectively, it works fine. When I use site- and year-specific covariates to model colonisation and extinction probabilities, my best model includes "connectivity" as an explanatory covariate for colonisation and "connectivity", "presence of wall lizards" and "vegetation cover" for extinction probabilities. However the SE's are huge, and all the P's are non-significant. The summary output looks like this:
 

Call:
colext(psiformula = ~connectivity + I(connectivity^2) + diameter+ structure length,
    gammaformula = ~connectivity, epsilonformula = ~connectivity+ presence_wall_lizards + 
    vegetation cover, pformula = ~Stemp + I(Stemp^2) + dur + wind, data = LaUMF, control = list(maxit = 100))
Initial (logit-scale):
                    Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)          6.967   3.696  1.88  0.05944
connectivity        10.404   4.765  2.18  0.02902
I(connectivity^2)   -4.278   1.987 -2.15  0.03128
diameter            -3.382   1.311 -2.58  0.00987
structure length     0.761   0.457  1.66  0.09619

Colonization (logit-scale):                 Estimate   SE       z    P(>|z|)
(Intercept)        -14.4   519  -0.0278   0.978
connectivity        10.8   520   0.0207   0.983

Extinction (logit-scale):
                        Estimate    SE      z      P(>|z|)
(Intercept)              14.1       14.6    0.967   0.333
connectivity            -218.8     215.3   -1.016   0.309
presence_wall_lizards    145.4     632.7    0.230   0.818
vegetation cover        -49.0       50.3   -0.975   0.330

Detection (logit-scale):
             Estimate    SE     z   P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    -1.222  0.139 -8.77  1.85e-18
Stemp           1.050  0.194  5.41  6.14e-08
I(Stemp^2)     -0.459  0.117 -3.93  8.55e-05
dur             0.751  0.124  6.07  1.30e-09
wind            0.370  0.116  3.18  1.48e-03

AIC: 529.3441
Number of sites: 76
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 170
Bootstrap iterations: 0
 
Reducing the extinction model leads to an increased AIC. My question: Does the likelihood function misbehave when the same covariates are used for occupancy and ext/col probabilities? Could anyone suggest any other reason for such high SE's?
 
Additionally I wanted to ask whether there is a R2-equivalent for unmarked models or any other way to extract the proportion of overall variation explained by a given model.
 
Since I'm quite new to unmarked, I'll appreciate any help or suggestions.
 
Many thanks!
Cristina

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Huge SE's when fitting colext models
parts:
Dear Cristina,

I would say that the huge SEs are a sign of either non-convergence, or more likely, of non-identifiability of the parameters for your data set. In principle, all such parameters should be identifiable, and in particular, it should not be a problem when you have the same covariates on different ones of the 4 logistic regressions that represents the dynocc model. However, with finite sample sizes you may well run into trouble.

The other question about the R2: This is non-trivial in a mixed model such as this one. I would say that with unmarked, you can't compute any R2-alike. In a Bayesian approach you could treat site- and/or year-effects as random and as coming from a normal distribution with a variance to be estimated (and no covariates). Then, you would fit the same model with some covariates. The proportional reduction in the site- or the year random effects variance could be interpreted as the proportion of the variance that is explained by that covariate(s). However, this is something that would have to be computed for each of the four logistic regressions separately.

Kind regards --  Marc

messages.author: 326ae5da9dd7e9d7
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Huge SE's when fitting colext models
parts:
Hi Marc,
 
Many thanks for your reply! I think it is really a problem of sample sizes. I calculated the extinction and colonisation probabilities using the estimates from the base model and I got very low values. The probability that colonisation and extincion events have occurred is therefore very low.  If there are no or too few colonisation or extinction events, they can't be explained by any covariates.
 
Thanks again for your comments.
 
Kind regards,
 
Cristina

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Huge SE's when fitting colext models
parts:
Additional comment:

Benedikt Schmidt just pointed out to me that you seem to have extreme colonisation and extinction values:

Here is the intercept for colonisation:
> plogis( -14.4)
[1] 5.573901e-07

And here the intercept for extinction:
> plogis(14.1)
[1] 0.9999992

I can't make sense of a dynamic system where there is essentially 100 chance of extinction, but whatever it is, it is not surprising to get weird SEs in such a situation.

Kind regards  --  Marc
